Item: People section has its own audit
Detail: Every person exists two or three times at two or three live URLs. Largest unresolved area of the rebuild; most of it waits on one editorial decision about which structure is canonical. See PEOPLE-AUDIT.md. Its 1,075 scraped pages are also the bulk of the nested-main count below

Only 679 distinct pages are ever linked to; the rest are reachable only by typing the URL. Concentrated in two places: 2,154 in /people/ (the duplicate structures) and 71 in /services/ (scraped Client Support Services). Everything else is a tail of about 38. Held out of search today only by the sitewide noindex

Scraped pages carry their own main element inside the one the template provides. Two mains means assistive tech cannot tell which is the main content, and the skip-to-content link may land in the wrong place. This is the de-scrape job proper - the largest single item on the list

Counted 2026-11-12. Concentrated in live's people-directory filters: /role/ 1142, /people-last-name/ 949, /most-recent-year-iqss/ 273, /people/ 218, /program/ 158, other 617. About three quarters exist only inside scraped person pages, so this shrinks with the People decision rather than needing its own pass

63 files link to /client-support-services/... - a whole retired section of live, not one page. Root-absolute so they 404 regardless. All 63 are themselves orphans: 58 sit in content/services/technology/, the scraped copy of that same retired section (62 unreachable pages for a team that no longer exists). Repointing them would polish pages nobody can reach; the section wants archiving instead

Item: Drupal staging host leaks into content
Detail: Links point at prod-harvardiqss.drupalsites.harvard.edu - Harvard's Drupal staging server, picked up by the scrape. Two are on the home page. They may work today and may stop without notice, and they advertise an internal host; they should point at the public address or at our own pages

Item: Site does not host its own images
Detail: The scrape took markup but not media. 1,223 tags point at /sites/g/files/... with no host and 404 on our site today; 1,048 point at www.iq.harvard.edu and load only while Harvard serves them. About 1,450 distinct files, 426 sharing a name with something already in static/images/. All 324 curated profiles hotlink their portrait; none holds its own. tools/fetch-live-images.ps1 will fetch them, but the firewall refuses non-browser clients - a Drupal media-library export is the better route and gets the masters rather than resized derivatives

Item: Two logos cost 228 KB on every page
Detail: Both are far larger than displayed, and both download on every visit on every device: each is hidden by CSS at the width where the other shows, and display:none does not stop a browser fetching an img. Every visitor pays for both and sees one. Highest-leverage image fix because it is on every page
Whose call: Liz to produce; Claude to wire
